gloss: to be intricate; to be complicated

forms.label: Past polite
forms.negative: {入|い}り{組|く}みませんでした

forms.label: ている past
forms.negative: {入|い}り{組|く}んでいなかった

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {入|い}り{組|く}んでいませんでした

definitions.gloss: to be intricate; to be complicated; to be complex
definitions.explanation: Describes something that is tangled, intertwined, or complicated in structure. Used for physical layouts (winding streets, coastlines) as well as abstract situations (complicated circumstances, relationships).

examples.japanese: {入|い}り{組|く}んだ{路地|ろじ}が{続|つづ}く。
examples.english: Intricate alleyways continue on and on.

examples.japanese: {事情|じじょう}が{入|い}り{組|く}んでいて{簡単|かんたん}には{説明|せつめい}できない。
examples.english: The circumstances are complicated and can't be explained simply.

examples.japanese: この{地域|ちいき}は{海岸線|かいがんせん}が{入|い}り{組|く}んでいるため、{港|みなと}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Because the coastline is intricate in this region, there are many harbors.

notes:
Almost always used in the ている form ({入|い}り{組|く}んでいる) to describe a state of being intricate or complicated. The past participle form {入|い}り{組|く}んだ is also common as a modifier: {入|い}り{組|く}んだ{問題|もんだい} (a complicated problem).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {入|い}り{組|く}んだ{事情|じじょう} — complicated circumstances
- {入|い}り{組|く}んだ{路地|ろじ} — intricate alleyways
- {入|い}り{組|く}んだ{関係|かんけい} — a tangled relationship
- {海岸線|かいがんせん}が{入|い}り{組|く}む — the coastline is jagged/indented
